records.name: Sibling Support Group (Philly HEALs)
records.summary: Free online group for people whose sibling died from a drug-related loss. The city's Philly HEALs program runs it.
records.what_you_do: Talk with other siblings about your loss, the people you miss, and how you keep going day to day.

schedule.text: Online sessions on Zoom. The one session listed on the Philly HEALs calendar is on a Thursday evening, 6:30 to 8 pm Eastern. The site does not give a repeating schedule.

first_step.how: Sign up through the city's online form to receive the Zoom link.
first_step.basis: Open to anyone who lost a sibling this way, with a clear online sign-up. The page does not describe a first session, so it is not rated higher.
first_step.what_to_expect: You sign up first, and the Zoom link is sent to you afterward. The session runs about an hour and a half, from 6:30 to 8 pm Eastern. The page does not say how many people attend or how the group is run.
first_visit_tips: Fill in the form before the session, because the Zoom link comes only after you sign up.
Call 215-516-9429 or email rachel.essy@phila.gov with questions before you join.

records.notes: The city page lists six other Philly HEALs support groups, which are in leads_only. The one-time session date was moved out of schedule.text. No form was submitted.

records.name: SIFTMedia 215 Collective
records.summary: A Philadelphia support network for women-identified and non-binary filmmakers, with workshops, screenings and mentoring for media artists.
records.what_you_do: Send a short note through the contact form to apply for membership, or subscribe to the newsletter. Then come to a listed workshop or screening. Donations help fund the group's film projects.

schedule.text: Workshops, screenings, a film club and general meetings are posted on the events page as they are planned. The page does not say which events are in person or online.

cost.text: No event prices or membership dues are listed on the site. Donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Apply for membership through the contact form on the group's site, then attend a listed workshop or screening.
first_step.basis: Listings are public and membership is open through a contact form with an email reply, but the site does not say beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: The events page lists workshops, screenings, a film club, and general meetings, usually with a date but often without a time, place, or price. Membership replies come by email, so ask about a listing's place and cost before you come.
first_visit_tips: Email contact@siftmediacollective.org or use the contact form to ask where an event is held and what it costs.
Check each listing for its date, since some show only a month and day.

records.notes: Membership applications run through the contact form. The site names no fee and no beginner wording. The mailing address on the contact page is a mail drop with a unit number, so it is not listed as a place to meet. The contact email comes from the group's own contact page and replaces the earlier address.

records.name: Singing City
records.summary: A Philadelphia choral group that says it has sung together since 1948. It has an adult choir that rehearses weekly from September through May, and a free youth program called Next Generation for young singers.
records.what_you_do: Adults send a request form to be considered for an audition, then rehearse and sing in the choir's four public concerts each season. Young singers can join the free Saturday youth program with no audition.

schedule.text: Adult choir rehearses on Tuesday evenings, 7:20 to 9:50 pm, at Friends Center from September through May, with occasional all-day Saturday rehearsals before big concerts. The youth program meets on Saturdays during the fall term: Youth Choir (ages 11 and under) at 11:15 am and Chorale (ages 12 and up) at 12:30 pm.

cost.text: The youth program is free. The site lists no adult membership or audition fee. Parking near Friends Center is $24 with a validation from the front desk, or $12 for evening parking two blocks away. Concert tickets are sold through Humanitix, and the concerts page does not list prices.

first_step.how: Adults: send the audition request form linked on the auditions page, since auditions are by invitation. Young singers: register for Next Generation through the link on the site, with no audition needed.
first_step.basis: The adult choir is by invitation after a request form, and the site lists sight-reading and prior choral experience as things that help. The youth program has open registration and no audition.
first_step.what_to_expect: Adults send a request form, then audition with one solo of their own choice, sight-reading, tonal memory checks, and vocal range exercises. Adult rehearsals are on Tuesday evenings at Friends Center. Youth singers join Saturday sessions with no audition, the program is free, and the young singers perform in a concert.
first_visit_tips: Bring a copy of your audition solo for the music director, who plays the accompaniment.
Get Friends Center parking validated at the front desk for $24, or use evening parking two blocks away for $12.

records.notes: Adult rehearsal times, season and parking come from the auditions page. The concerts page lists four concerts for 2026 and 2027, and the fall concert on October 25, 2026 sets the sign of life month. The youth page does not say Presser Hall is the Temple Music Prep site named in the earlier record, so that label was replaced.

records.name: Sisters Giving Back
records.summary: A community nonprofit, started in 2011, that helps girls and young women build confidence, plan for college, and grow into leaders. It gives scholarships and runs leadership programs and yearly conferences.
records.what_you_do: Register for the six-month leadership cohort or the STEM conference through the online forms on the group's site. Women who want to help can join as members to mentor and fundraise. Three scholarships a year go to first-year college students, and applications are accepted through April 30, 2027.

schedule.text: The teen girls conference is held each October. The scholarship gala is held each spring. Other programs are posted on the upcoming events page with their own dates.

cost.text: The site lists no prices for the cohort or the conferences, and no membership fee is stated.

first_step.how: Register for the STEM Conference on Saturday, November 21, 2026, through the registration form on the group's site, or send the membership form to join as a volunteer mentor.
first_step.basis: Events and membership have clear online sign-up forms, and nothing requires an invitation. The site does not describe what a first event is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The STEM conference runs from 9:30 am to 4 pm on a Saturday at Temple University's Morgan Hall. Past teen girls conferences have included workshops on confidence, fashion, and social media, plus skits and public speaking. The site does not list prices or describe a first event.
first_visit_tips: Fill in the online registration form ahead of time, since events and the cohort sign up online.
Morgan Hall is on Temple University's campus at 1700 N. Broad Street.
The leadership cohort meets at Universal Institute Charter School, 1415 Catherine Street.

records.notes: The newest teen girls conference recap is from November 2025, and no 2026 conference date is posted yet. Membership is described as volunteer mentoring and fundraising for women, not as a program for girls. The website has no accessibility notes.

records.name: Sisters in Strength
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that works to empower women and girls through education, arts and culture, sports, and health programs. It also runs a summer camp.
records.what_you_do: Girls and women can take part in the group's programs and its summer camp, which the site says serves ages 6 to 24. The website does not explain how to enroll, so call or email to ask.

schedule.text: The website lists a summer camp, but gives no dates, hours, or grades for it. Ask the office for the current schedule.

cost.text: The website does not list a cost for the summer camp or the programs.

first_step.how: Call 215-971-0918 or email info@sistersinstrength23.org during office hours to ask about the summer camp and how to join.
first_step.basis: The site gives no sign-up steps for programs or the camp, so the way in is unclear and you need to contact the office first.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit. The summer camp is described as a program that builds confidence, creativity, and friendships for young people ages 6 to 24. The page says the camp is meant to be affordable and open, and it gives no fee.
first_visit_tips: Call during office hours: Monday to Friday 9 am to 6 pm, and Saturday 10 am to 4 pm.
Ask the office for the summer camp's dates, hours, and fees, since the website lists none.

records.notes: The site has no camp dates, prices, enrollment steps, or accessibility notes. The camp page footer shows 2023, which is not counted as evidence. One web search for public listings of the camp found nothing relevant. The contact page also lists strengthsinsisters@gmail.com, which is not used here.

records.name: Skate The Foundry
records.summary: A skate school in West Philadelphia that teaches skateboarding and roller skating to kids, teens, and adults, with after-school, weekend, and camp options and open skate time.
records.what_you_do: Kids can join a Thursday after-school skateboard club, Saturday youth classes, or camps on school days off and in the summer. Walk-in open skate is for skaters with at least six months of riding experience. The site does not list volunteer roles.

schedule.text: Thursday after-school club from 4:30 to 6:30 pm. Saturday youth classes in the morning and early afternoon. Open skate on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday from 4 to 9 pm, and on Thursday from 6:30 to 9 pm (hours listed for spring 2026). Camps run on school days off, and summer camps are held at Paine's Park.

cost.text: Paid programs. Recent listings show youth Saturday classes at $390 per round, the after-school club at $420 per six-session round (includes a $20 registration fee), open skate at $10 a day (members skate free), summer camp at $600 a week in 2026, and holiday day camp at $130 a day. Club gear rental is $5 per class. New students get 15 percent off a first private lesson.

requirements.gear: Bring a traditional skateboard (penny boards and longboards are not allowed), a helmet, and knee, elbow and wrist pads. Club board and safety gear can be rented for $5 per class.

first_step.how: New skaters book one to three private lessons first, then register for a class round through the Register Here links on the class pages.
first_step.basis: The FAQ says total beginners are welcome, and there is a beginner kids class and a new student discount. Walk-in open skate needs six months of riding first.
first_step.what_to_expect: The school suggests that a total beginner takes one to three private lessons before joining a class. Youth Saturday classes run about 75 minutes with up to 10 skaters, and parents are asked to step out during class. Open skate is a walk-in session for skaters with at least six months of regular riding, and you sign a waiver when you arrive.
first_visit_tips: Book a private lesson or a class round online before you come, since walk-ins are only welcome at open skate.
Bring a traditional skateboard, a helmet, and knee, elbow and wrist pads, or rent safety gear for $5 per class at the club.
Parents are asked to step out during class and may come back 5 to 10 minutes before it ends.
Check the school's social media for open skate schedule changes before you go.

records.notes: Open skate hours are from the spring 2026 listing, and prices are from the 2025 and 2026 round listings. Gear notes in the FAQ that refer to 2020 Covid rules were left out. A separate skate shop in Elkins Park is outside the city and was not added as a location. Payments are non-refundable, and camp cancellation credit depends on how much notice is given.

records.name: Skateboard Academy of Philadelphia
records.summary: A skateboarding school that offers private and group lessons, camps and community sessions for all levels. It also runs Open World Skate, a skateboarding program built on ABA therapy.
records.what_you_do: Book a lesson or community session through the contact form on the website. For Open World Skate, a program built on ABA therapy, the site says to contact the partner behavioral service named on the page to start intake. It also says coaches are certified ABA therapists or are training to become one.

schedule.text: Community sessions run on Saturdays and Sundays at the D Street location, and the site does not publish times. Private lessons, group lessons, and camps are also offered, with prices not listed.

cost.text: Prices are not on the site. A membership is advertised to save money, but no amount is listed. Camp and community session prices are not stated.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the website to request a lesson or community session.
first_step.basis: The site says all levels and abilities are welcome and gives a booking form, though it does not describe a first visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit. It says the school teaches people of all ages and levels, and that its lessons use ABA methods such as set routines, positive feedback, and progress tracking. Open World Skate is a separate program with its own intake.
first_visit_tips: Book through the contact form, since online booking is still listed as coming soon.
The site links a waiver page, so read and sign it before your first session.

records.notes: theskateboardacademy.com answers with a 301 to radworldnj.com/the-skateboard-academy, which is the same group's page, so it was followed. The footer names Rad World NJ as operator, and the founder bio ties the academy to SK8 Edu. The social links on that page belong to Rad World Skatepark, so they are not listed here. The schedule page linked from the site showed no entries. No phone, email, prices, or times are published.
